name: csv
doc: CSV parsing and writing (RFC 4180 quoting). All cell values are strings when parsing; a leading UTF-8 byte-order mark is ignored. Rows may have differing lengths. Unknown option names raise an error.

functions.name: parse

params.name: s
params.doc: CSV text.

params.name: opts
params.doc: {header = true, delimiter = ",", trim = false}. With header = true each row is a table keyed by the header names (empty names become column_N, duplicates get _2, _3 suffixes; short rows are padded with empty strings, extra cells are named column_N). With header = false rows are arrays of strings. trim = true strips surrounding whitespace from every cell. delimiter must be a single character.

functions.doc: Parses all of s into an array of rows. On malformed CSV returns nil and a message of the form "line N: message".
functions.example:
local rows, err = csv.parse("name,qty\nbolt,3\n")
return rows[1].name  -- "bolt"

functions.name: rows

params.name: s
params.doc: CSV text.

params.name: opts
params.doc: {header = true, delimiter = ",", trim = false}. With header = true each row is a table keyed by the header names (empty names become column_N, duplicates get _2, _3 suffixes; short rows are padded with empty strings, extra cells are named column_N). With header = false rows are arrays of strings. trim = true strips surrounding whitespace from every cell. delimiter must be a single character.

functions.doc: Returns an iterator yielding one row per call, for use in a generic for loop. Malformed CSV raises an error when the bad line is reached.
functions.example:
for row in csv.rows(text) do
  total = total + tonumber(row.qty)
end

functions.name: encode

params.name: rows
params.doc: Array of rows. Each row is an array of values, or a table keyed by column name (then opts.columns is required).

params.name: opts
params.doc: {columns = {"a", "b"}, delimiter = ",", header = true}. columns selects and orders keyed-row cells and supplies the header line. For array rows a header line is written only when columns is given. Cells may be strings, numbers, booleans, decimals, nil or db.NULL (empty).

errors: result exceeds the maximum string size (SCRIPT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED)
functions.doc: Encodes rows as CSV text with LF line endings and standard quoting.

name: datetime
doc: Dates and times. A timestamp is an ISO 8601 UTC string like "2026-03-09T05:30:00.000Z"; a date is "2026-01-31". Timestamps and dates are plain strings, so they sort and compare correctly with < and ==. Calendar arithmetic and local-time parsing use the workspace time zone unless a tz argument is given. Invalid tz names raise an error.

functions.name: now
functions.doc: Returns the current time as an ISO UTC timestamp (millisecond precision).

functions.name: today

params.name: tz
params.doc: IANA time zone name such as "America/New_York". Defaults to the workspace time zone.

functions.doc: Returns today's date (YYYY-MM-DD) in the time zone.

functions.name: parse

params.name: s
params.doc: RFC 3339 (any offset), "YYYY-MM-DD" (midnight in tz), "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM" or "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS" (local time in tz).

params.name: tz
params.doc: IANA time zone name such as "America/New_York". Defaults to the workspace time zone.

functions.doc: Parses a date/time into an ISO UTC timestamp. On failure returns nil and an error message instead of raising.
functions.example:
local ts, err = datetime.parse("2026-03-08 21:30", "America/New_York")
if not ts then error(err) end

functions.name: format

params.name: ts
params.doc: A timestamp or date (any form accepted by datetime.parse).

params.name: layout
params.doc: strftime-style layout. Supported: %Y %m %d %H %M %S %y %b %B %a %A %p %I %j %Z %z %%.

params.name: tz
params.doc: IANA time zone name such as "America/New_York". Defaults to the workspace time zone.

errors: result exceeds the maximum string size (SCRIPT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED)
functions.doc: Formats a time in the time zone. %Z is the zone abbreviation and %z the numeric offset such as +0100.

functions.name: add

params.name: ts
params.doc: A timestamp or date.

params.name: spec
params.doc: Any of years, months, days, weeks (whole numbers, may be negative) and hours, minutes, seconds (fractions allowed).

params.name: tz
params.doc: IANA time zone name such as "America/New_York". Defaults to the workspace time zone.

functions.doc: Adds calendar and clock amounts. years, months, days and weeks use calendar arithmetic in the time zone so local clock time is kept across daylight-saving changes; adding months clamps to the end of shorter months (Jan 31 + 1 month = Feb 28). hours, minutes and seconds are exact elapsed time. When ts is a date and only years/months/days/weeks are given the result is a date, otherwise a timestamp.

functions.name: diff

params.name: a
params.doc: Start timestamp or date.

params.name: b
params.doc: End timestamp or date.

params.name: unit
params.doc: One of "seconds", "minutes", "hours", "days", "weeks", "months", "years".

params.name: tz
params.doc: IANA time zone name such as "America/New_York". Defaults to the workspace time zone.

errors: a or b cannot be parsed
functions.doc: Returns b - a in the unit. seconds to weeks are exact elapsed time (a day is 24 hours) and may be fractional. months and years count whole calendar months/years in the time zone, truncated toward zero.

name: db
doc: Run SQL against this workspace's tables. Reads run on a snapshot; writes need edit rights and are not recorded in row history (use `records` for tracked edits). Statements are checked by the SQL authorizer: system tables, schema changes, PRAGMA and ATTACH are not allowed.

functions.name: query

params.name: sql
params.doc: One read-only statement; use :name placeholders.

params.name: params
params.doc: Values for :name placeholders.

functions.returns: array of row tables keyed by column name (SQL NULL is db.NULL)
functions.doc: Runs a read-only query and returns up to 10,000 rows.
functions.example: local rows = db.query("SELECT Name FROM Customers WHERE City = :city", {city = "Paris"})

functions.name: query_one
functions.doc: Like db.query but returns only the first row.
functions.example: local c = db.query_one("SELECT * FROM Customers WHERE id = :id", {id = 1})

functions.name: query_value
functions.returns: first column of the first row, or nil when there are no rows
functions.doc: Returns a single value.
functions.example: local n = db.query_value("SELECT count(*) FROM Orders")

functions.name: iter
functions.doc: Iterates over a large result in pages of 1,000 rows (jobs only).
functions.example: for row in db.iter("SELECT * FROM Orders") do total = total + row.Qty end

functions.name: exec
functions.doc: Runs one INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE on a workspace table. Not available in reports.
functions.example: db.exec("UPDATE Orders SET Status = 'Shipped' WHERE id = :id", {id = 7})

functions.name: transaction
functions.doc: Runs fn inside one write transaction (all-or-nothing). Raising an error inside fn rolls back. The block has its own time budget (250 ms in form events, 2 s in jobs).
functions.example: db.transaction(function() db.exec("UPDATE Stock SET Qty = Qty - 1 WHERE id = :id", {id = 3}) records.insert("Moves", {Item = 3}) end)

functions.name: lookup
functions.doc: Access DLookup: the field's value in the first matching row, or db.NULL.

functions.name: count
functions.doc: Access DCount: number of matching rows (non-empty values of field, or all rows when field is "*" or omitted).

functions.name: sum
functions.doc: Access DSum.

functions.name: avg
functions.doc: Access DAvg.

functions.doc: Access DMin.

functions.doc: True for nil and db.NULL.

name: decimal
doc:
Exact base-10 arithmetic. Currency is stored as an integer scaled by 10^4 and appears in scripts as decimal values, so decimal.new("0.1") + decimal.new("0.2") == decimal.new("0.3") is true.

Decimals support + - * / % unary minus, == < <= > >= and .. (concatenation). Arithmetic operands may be decimals, numbers (converted through their shortest exact decimal representation) or numeric strings. Lua 5.1 caveats: == is only evaluated when both sides are decimals, so decimal == number is always false; < <= > >= only work between two decimals and comparing a decimal with a number raises an error. Convert first: d == decimal.new(1), d < decimal.new("2.5"). Division keeps 16 decimal places and raises on division by zero; % follows Lua (the result has the sign of the divisor). Values are limited to about 4,900 digits and an exponent of 1000.

Decimal values have the methods d:round(places), d:tostring() and d:tonumber().

functions.name: new

params.name: value
params.doc: A numeric string such as "12.50" or "1e3", a finite number, or another decimal.

errors: value is not a number, numeric string or decimal
the string is not a valid decimal or is too large
functions.doc: Creates a decimal. Prefer strings for exact values; a number is converted through its shortest round-trip representation, so decimal.new(0.1) is exactly 0.1.

functions.name: is_decimal

params.name: value
params.doc: Any value.

functions.doc: Returns true when value is a decimal.

name: fetch
doc: Makes an HTTP request from a job. Only hosts and ports on the platform's egress allowlist, which platform administrators manage for all workspaces, are reachable (https unless the platform also allows http); an empty allowlist permits nothing; private and internal addresses are always refused, including after redirects (at most 5).

functions.name: fetch
functions.signature: fetch(url, {method, headers, body, timeout_ms, max_bytes}?) → response

params.name: url
params.doc: Absolute https URL.

params.name: options
params.doc: method (default GET); headers (string → string); body (string); timeout_ms (default 10000, at most 30000); max_bytes (default 2 MiB, at most 10 MiB).

functions.returns: {status, ok, headers, body, json()}: ok is true for 2xx; header names are lower-case; response:json() decodes the body like json.decode.
errors: EGRESS_DENIED: host, port or address not allowed
RATE_LIMITED: too many requests from this workspace
functions.doc: Sends the request and reads the whole response.
functions.example:
local r = fetch("https://api.example.com/rates", {headers = {Accept = "application/json"}})
if r.ok then log.info("rates", {count = #r:json().items}) end

params.name: name
params.doc: Job name.

params.name: args
params.doc: Arguments merged over the job's own args (string keys; JSON-compatible values).

functions.returns: The new run's id. The run starts as soon as a worker is free, following the job's overlap policy.
errors: NOT_FOUND: no job with that name
FORBIDDEN: the job does not allow enqueue from forms
WORKSPACE_BUSY: the job is already running (overlap policy)
functions.doc: Queues a run of a job. From a form, the user must be an editor or above and the job's args must contain allow_enqueue = true.

name: json
doc:
JSON encoding and decoding.

Encoding rules: tables with keys exactly 1..n (n >= 1) or marked with json.array become arrays; an empty unmarked table becomes {}; other tables become objects with sorted keys (keys must be strings or numbers). json.null and db.NULL become null; decimals become JSON strings. Integral numbers within +/-2^53 are written without a decimal point; NaN and infinity raise. Nesting deeper than 100 levels and cycles raise.

Decoding maps objects to tables, arrays to tables marked as arrays (so they re-encode as arrays even when empty), null to json.null, and integers beyond +/-2^53 to strings to avoid precision loss.

json.array and json.object mark a table by giving it a private metatable. Calling setmetatable on a marked table replaces the metatable and drops the mark.

functions.name: encode

params.name: value
params.doc: The value to encode.

params.name: opts
params.doc: {pretty = boolean}: pretty = true indents with two spaces.

errors: unsupported value type (function, thread, non-null userdata)
table keys that are not strings or numbers
nesting deeper than 100 or cyclic tables
result exceeds the maximum string size (SCRIPT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED)
functions.doc: Encodes a Lua value as JSON text.

functions.name: decode

params.name: s
params.doc: JSON text.

functions.doc: Parses JSON text. On invalid JSON returns nil and an error message instead of raising. A literal null decodes to json.null (not nil).
functions.example:
local v, err = json.decode('{"a":[1,2,null]}')
if not v then error(err) end

functions.name: array

params.name: t
params.doc: Table to mark; a new empty table when omitted.

functions.doc: Marks t (and returns it) so it always encodes as a JSON array, even when empty. Keys other than 1..n make encoding fail.

functions.name: object

params.name: t
params.doc: Table to mark; a new empty table when omitted.

functions.doc: Marks t (and returns it) so it always encodes as a JSON object, including an empty table or one with integer keys. Overrides json.array.

values.name: null
values.doc: The JSON null value. Compare with ==; it is distinct from nil and db.NULL but both encode as null.

name: staging
doc:
Scratch tables for bulk loads. staging.create returns a handle with these methods; the staging tables are private to the run and deleted when it ends (at most 8 per run, 1,000,000 rows and 256 MiB each).

handle:insert(row): adds one row, given as a table keyed by column name or as an array in column order. Values are text, numbers, booleans or db.NULL; missing columns are empty.

handle:query(sql, params?) → rows: runs one SELECT against the table, which is named data (columns are the names given to create, plus n, the insertion number). Use ? placeholders with an array or :name placeholders with a table. Writes, PRAGMA, ATTACH and any other table are refused (SQL_NOT_ALLOWED). Returns an array of row tables keyed by column name; SQL NULL is db.NULL. A result of more than 100,000 rows or 32 MiB is an error.

handle:count() → number: the number of rows inserted.

handle:merge_into(table_name, {mode, key, chunk, all_or_nothing}?) → {inserted, updated, skipped, error_count, errors}: copies every row into the table. Staging column names must match the table's field names (display or physical name, any case). mode is "append" (default), "upsert" (key = the name of a field with a unique index; existing rows with the same key are updated) or "replace" (delete all rows, then insert; one transaction up to 50,000 rows). Rows are converted exactly like row API values (text "12.50" for currency, ISO dates, yes/no words) and written in chunks of chunk rows (default 2,000, at most 10,000) so interactive saves are served between chunks; rows the database rejects are skipped and listed in errors (the first 100, each {row, column, code, message}). With all_or_nothing = true the whole merge is one transaction that rolls back on the first bad row and raises an error. merge_into cannot run inside db.transaction.

functions.name: create

params.name: options
params.doc: columns: array of column names (letters, digits, underscores; at most 256; n is reserved).

functions.returns: A staging handle with the methods insert, query, count and merge_into (see the module description).
errors: BAD_REQUEST: invalid or repeated column names
QUOTA_EXCEEDED: too many staging tables in this run
functions.doc: Creates an empty staging table for this run.
functions.example:
local st = staging.create({columns = {"sku", "qty"}})
st:insert({sku = "A-1", qty = 5})
st:insert({"B-2", 7})
local rows = st:query("SELECT sku FROM data WHERE qty > :min", {min = 5})
local res = st:merge_into("Stock", {mode = "upsert", key = "sku"})
log.info("merged", {inserted = res.inserted, updated = res.updated})
